newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Thirty killed in tide of Colombian violence.
newsitem.headline: Thirty killed in tide of Colombian violence.

text.p: Thirty people died in a two-day wave of political bloodshed across Colombia capped by a rebel attack in the capital early on Friday in which two security force members were killed, authorities said.

Police and military officials said the victims of the attacks between early Thursday and Friday afternoon included 10 people -- among them a 3-year-old child -- killed by a bomb detonated by Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels on Thursday morning in the northwest banana-growing region of Uraba.
Others included four civilians gunned down by a suspected right-wing paramilitary group in northern Sucre province and 12 guerrillas and two police killed in gunfights around the country.

Also, two policemen were killed in a FARC assault early on Thursday on the mountain town of Labranzagrande in central Boyaca province, and two Colombian marines were killed when suspected FARC urban commandos sprayed their sentry post outside a naval office in the capital with automatic gunfire early on Friday.
The FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest rebel group, was founded as a Marxist-led pro-Soviet guerrilla army in 1964.
